Subject: Invoice question — GST treatment and split for Q2

Hi Sergio,

Hope you’re well. We received Redwood’s Q2 invoice but our AP team has placed it on hold because of how the GST was applied. BrightTrail is registered for GST in Singapore and we need the invoice split between the platform charge (B2B reverse-charge) and the professional services item (subject to SG GST) so our accounting system can map to the correct tax codes.

Can you confirm:
- Whether Redwood treated the platform usage as reverse-charge (place of supply outside SG) or charged SG GST on the token usage line?
- If reverse-charge was used, can you provide evidence of Redwood’s non-resident status / place of supply determination (snapshot of GST registration guidance or tax memo)?

We can re-release payment once we receive a corrected invoice or supporting evidence.

Thanks — please loop in your tax/finance contact.

Regards,
Anika Shah
Accounts Payable
BrightTrail Logistics

Hi Anika — thank you for the note and the PO. Sorry for the hassle.

Quick summary: for BrightTrail’s account we applied a split invoice because some line items are platform consumption (hosted inference) while others were professional services (onboarding and integration). For APAC SG-registered customers we typically treat the platform usage as place-of-supply outside Singapore (reverse-charge) when the customer is GST-registered and provides a valid GST number; professional services delivered in SG are charged SG GST.

To unblock payment immediately I’ve attached a split PDF (part A = platform, part B = services) and a checklist of the evidence we need from you to confirm reverse-charge:
- Copy of BrightTrail’s SG GST registration (snapshot or certificate)
- Confirmation that the billing entity on your side is the SG-registered entity (legal name + UEN)
- PO referencing the invoice (you attached PO_7781 — thanks)

Mina — can you confirm the language we should include on the invoice (reverse-charge wording + tax note) and whether we need to route for an amendment? Marcus / Priya — FYI on the PO mapping and manual payment release if we accept the evidence.

Attachments: 2026-Q2-invoice-part-A.pdf (split invoice), BTL_GST_registration_snapshot.png (incoming placeholder)

Best,
Sergio
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>, Anika Shah <ap@brighttraillogistics.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Apr 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Invoice question — GST treatment and split for Q2

Thanks Sergio / Anika — adding the tax ops note here.

Anika — we reviewed the initial billing and the split looks appropriate. For administrative clarity on the invoice we will: 1) mark the platform consumption line as zero-rated under reverse-charge with the following note: "Recipient obligated to account for GST under Singapore reverse-charge rules; supplier not charging GST." 2) Charge SG GST on the services line at the statutory rate and include our company details + tax residency statement.

Evidence required from BrightTrail (please send as PDF/png):
- Official GST registration snapshot showing the UEN and GST registration number
- Confirmation that the paying entity is the same legal entity listed on the GST cert (if different, provide inter-company agreement)

If you can send those two items to us by EOD Thursday, we’ll reissue the invoice with the exact reverse-charge wording and accelerate manual payment release. If not, we can provide a debit/credit split memo but AP will need to hold until verification is completed.

Note to internal team: once we have the docs I’ll prepare the amended invoice in SAP and run a one-off settlement for this PO. Marcus — please hold any automated dunning for 7 days.

Mina Haddad
Tax & Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
